The common partner spreadsheet is Account + Contact denormalised into 25 columns with repeated company data — recognising that repetition ('does column set A repeat across rows keyed by column set B?') is the judgement call that decides whether this is one load or two, and the playbook never prompts it.

One-time load or recurring feed? `skills/data/etl-vs-api-data-patterns` is read for exactly this ('decides whether the mapping should be a CSV load at all'), and no Plan step consults it. Recurring changes everything: it makes the External ID mandatory rather than nice-to-have, and it makes the answer 'build an integration' rather than 'map a CSV'.

Choosing DateTime for a birthdate shifts every value by the user's timezone offset; and the playbook never states what date format the CSV must be in for the chosen loader. Process Observations mentions 'columns with embedded delimiters (common with copied Excel)' as something to notice after the fact, but no Plan step asks about encoding, BOM, quoting or embedded newlines — the failures that stop the load before field mapping matters at all.

Neither the agent, the command wrapper, nor the decision tree (grepped: no 'delta' or 'incremental' branch in all 210 lines) ever raises it.

Rollback and reconciliation. There is no step for it anywhere. Nothing computes the plan's consumption against the org's allocations: 150,000,000 Bulk records per rolling 24 hours, 15,000 batches per 24 hours (both verified in the Salesforce limits cheatsheet), and the daily API request allocation shared with every other integration. Everything that happens org-side when 8M Accounts land. assessments.weakest_aspect: It carries the batch's only wrong Salesforce facts, in the security section, where wrong facts do damage. Step 5 says to use Guest User Sharing Rules rather than Sharing Sets because 'guest users have no User record to chain from' — the rationale is false. Guest users do have a User record; what they lack is an associated Contact, and the operative constraint is the 'Secure guest user record access' setting, which per Salesforce Help is enabled by default and cannot be disabled, blocks guest users from queues, public groups, manual sharing, and Apex managed sharing, and permits record access only through guest user sharing rules. A model that internalises 'no User record' will make wrong downstream calls about ownership, FLS, and the guest profile. Worse, the agent never states the fact that most changes a design: guest user sharing rules grant Read Only access, full stop. Step 5 then invites the model to 'propose the minimal CRUD shape' for guest submissions without that ceiling in view. Separately, the audit row 'Partner Community with member role hierarchy depth > 5 (performance risk) | P1' describes a configuration that cannot exist — partner account roles default to 1 and cap at 3 — so the finding can never fire and the number is fabricated. Every one of those templates falls through all four classification branches unclassified. Meanwhile the Lightning branch keys off `TemplateStyle = freeform`, but freeForm is a Classic TemplateStyle value too, so Classic templates get scored as modern. The actual Classic/Lightning discriminator on EmailTemplate (the UiType field) is never mentioned.
